chapter: Willy Lewis band in Paris and Egypt
title: A pasha's invitation and harem
summary: A pasha entertained Butler at his home with couscous and showed his harem, urging him to learn Arabic and stay, as Egypt would soon be free of England.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: This was a man, he was a big Kahib but they didn't call them Kahib in Egypt, they called them Pashas, so this pasha, took me to his home, had his wives and he had two or three who was brunette who were right close to him and he served cous-cous and we ate and he said I want you to look at my harem. Do you like any of them. I said, yes, they're very beautiful.

He said well if you get lonely, you can -- I said, I didn't bring nothing here and I don't intend taking nothing out. That is Egyptian law. I said, yes, sir, I don't know that it's my law. He said, that's all right, don't worry about it. He said, but I want you to go to school and learn the Arab language because I want you to stay here. I want you to stay here,
because we are going to be free from England soon and we need people like you to run, to be in high places. So he was happy all the time.
